The line must go left: the door down is locked until its key is collected.
Going to number 2 leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (right from cell (2,1)) was wrong, so the line must go down.
I can't rule out down or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5); going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So my guess (down from cell (3,1)) was wrong, so the line must go right.

Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going up would wall in number 8, the last number. So the line goes left.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
